app.title: vizarr: multiscale OME-Zarr image viewer
app.summary: A person opens an image by putting the address of a Zarr, OME-Zarr, OME-TIFF or reference store in the page URL, or by adding a store from a Python notebook. The image appears in a pan-and-zoom canvas that loads only the resolution level and tiles in view, and a floating layer panel lets them set layer opacity, step through the time and z planes, and add, remove, recolour and set contrast for each channel in a blended composite. Segmentation label layers can be switched on and faded. A plate or well opens as a grid of fields that can be filtered by acquisition, and clicking a field opens that image in a new window. The current zoom and position are written back into the URL, so a view can be shared or picked up again.

task.text: Look closely at large, multi-channel, multi-dimensional microscopy images by blending chosen channels and stepping through planes, at any zoom.

data.text: Multiscale n-dimensional image arrays (time, channel, z, y, x) stored as chunked pyramids, with rendering metadata for each channel, optional segmentation label images, and plate or well collections of fields.
data.item: one multiscale image, or one field in a well on a plate

stage.text: looking over acquired microscopy images before analysis

mechanism.text: A GPU canvas draws the image tile by tile at the resolution level the zoom needs, blending each selected channel in its own colour and contrast window. A collapsible layer panel holds an accordion per image whose sliders and popovers rewrite that layer's channel selections, contrast limits, colours, label opacity and axis indices, and the canvas redraws at once. Plates are drawn as a grid of fields, where a click opens one field on its own, and the view state is kept in sync with the URL.

field.text: multiscale, multiplexed bioimage visualization in microscopy

workflow.name: open a large layered image and adjust how each layer is shown

steps.here: A store address goes in the ?source URL parameter (ome-tiff:// and ref:// prefixes pick other store types), or a notebook calls add_image with a zarr array, group or store, which is streamed through the widget.

steps.step: move around the image at any scale
steps.here: Pan and zoom on an orthographic canvas that fetches only the visible tiles from the right pyramid level. The view state is saved into the URL as you go.

steps.step: choose which channels to blend, with colour and contrast for each
steps.here: The + button adds a channel from the named list (up to a maximum). For each channel, a ring toggles it, a range slider sets the contrast window, and the ⋯ popover changes which channel it shows, the slider bounds, the colour from a palette, or removes it.
Each non-spatial axis (T, Z and others) has a slider showing index/max, plus a ⋯ box for typing an exact index. It applies to every channel at once.

steps.step: overlay annotations and set how strongly they show
steps.here: Segmentation label layers are listed under 'labels:', each with an on/off ring and an opacity slider. The image layer has its own opacity slider and an eye toggle.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A plate or well is drawn as a grid of field images with their names. A dropdown filters it to one acquisition.
Clicking a field in the plate grid opens that well image as its own source in a new window.

distinctive: Pyramidal multiscale images are streamed chunk by chunk from remote or notebook-backed stores, so images far larger than memory can be viewed entirely in the browser.
Channel composites are blended additively on the GPU, with a colour and a contrast window for each channel, and contrast is estimated from the lowest resolution level when the metadata gives none.
n-dimensional arrays are reduced to a 2D slice by one index per extra axis (time, z), shared across all channels.
It reads the community OME-NGFF metadata (multiscales, omero, plate, well, labels, coordinate transformations) across spec versions.
The view state is kept in the URL, so a view can be shared.
